trust_decision.summary: A stored PERMISSIONS WHERE predicate (definer-authored) is evaluated with permission enforcement disabled (new_with_perms(false) / skip_fetch_perms); whether that evaluation may run data-modifying statements is decided nowhere at the pinned commit. The fix adds a runtime guard in Expr::compute keyed on Options::permission_predicate plus definition-time rejection (has_direct_write) in DEFINE statements.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'table permissions'; this is the legacy table-permission check that computes the Specific predicate with new_with_perms(false) for SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE on records.

An over-broad fix keyed on perms==false (or rejecting any function call / subquery at DEFINE) breaks these.
